readback.mathematical_statement: The implicit geometric context has independent universes u_1,u_2,u_3: a real normed vector space E : Type u_1, a topological model H : Type u_2, an arbitrary ModelWithCorners I over R from E to H, and a topological M : Type u_3 with ChartedSpace H M and IsManifold I 1 M. The order 1 is in WithTop ENat. There is no completeness, finite-dimensionality, Hausdorffness, compactness, connectivity, boundarylessness or smooth-infinity requirement in this context. MetricCompatibleAt takes an explicit tangent-bilinear-form family g, an explicit CovariantDerivative on the tangent family and a point x, and defines a proposition. For every implicit tangent sections Y,Z that are manifold differentiable at x as their total-space sections, and every explicit v in the tangent space at x, it requires D_I(y |-> g(y)(Y(y),Z(y)))(x)[v] = g(x)((cov Y x)(v),Z(x)) + g(x)(Y(x),(cov Z x)(v)). Here D_I is mvfderiv I, the scalar directional derivative obtained by composing mfderiv I I(R,R) with the canonical continuous linear map from the scalar target tangent space to R, exactly as expanded in the snapshot. Differentiability is only at x, not global C1 of Y,Z. Each g(y) is a continuous bilinear form on its fiber, but this definition imposes no separate smoothness/continuity-in-y, symmetry, positivity or nondegeneracy premise on g. It is a pointwise compatibility predicate for supplied data and constructs no connection.

readback.name: CovariantDerivative.leviCivita_unique_at
readback.mathematical_statement: The implicit geometric context has independent universes u_1,u_2,u_3: a real normed vector space E : Type u_1, a topological model H : Type u_2, an arbitrary ModelWithCorners I over R from E to H, and a topological M : Type u_3 with ChartedSpace H M and IsManifold I 1 M. The order 1 is in WithTop ENat. There is no completeness, finite-dimensionality, Hausdorffness, compactness, connectivity, boundarylessness or smooth-infinity requirement in this context. For implicit fiberwise continuous real bilinear-form family g, implicit tangent connections cov,cov' and implicit x : M, suppose g(x) is symmetric and left-nondegenerate, meaning that if g(x)(v,w)=0 for every w then v=0. Assume MetricCompatibleAt g cov x and MetricCompatibleAt g cov' x, and TorsionFreeAt cov x and TorsionFreeAt cov' x. Then, for every implicit tangent section sigma that is manifold differentiable at x as a total-space section, cov.toFun sigma x = cov'.toFun sigma x as continuous linear maps from the tangent fiber at x to itself. This is pointwise uniqueness on differentiable sections, not equality of the whole connection records, equality at all points without the premises, or behavior on arbitrary nondifferentiable sections. Positive definiteness, smoothness of g and global C1 of the test sections are not separately assumed; symmetric nondegenerate forms may be indefinite. The theorem constructs no Levi-Civita connection.

readback.name: CovariantDerivative.koszul_formula
readback.mathematical_statement: The implicit geometric context has independent universes u_1,u_2,u_3: a real normed vector space E : Type u_1, a topological model H : Type u_2, an arbitrary ModelWithCorners I over R from E to H, and a topological M : Type u_3 with ChartedSpace H M and IsManifold I 1 M. The order 1 is in WithTop ENat. There is no completeness, finite-dimensionality, Hausdorffness, compactness, connectivity, boundarylessness or smooth-infinity requirement in this context. For implicit g, implicit tangent connection cov and implicit x, assume g(x) is symmetric, MetricCompatibleAt g cov x and TorsionFreeAt cov x. For implicit tangent sections X,Y,Z, each manifold differentiable at x as a total-space section, the Koszul identity holds: 2*g(x)((cov Y x)(X(x)),Z(x)) = D_I(g(Y,Z))(x)[X(x)] + D_I(g(X,Z))(x)[Y(x)] - D_I(g(X,Y))(x)[Z(x)] + g(x)([X,Y](x),Z(x)) - g(x)([X,Z](x),Y(x)) - g(x)([Y,Z](x),X(x)). Here g(A,B) denotes the scalar function y |-> g(y)(A(y),B(y)), each bracket is mlieBracket I, each D_I is the explicit scalar fromTangentSpace-composed mfderiv with model I, and 2 is real. Unlike the uniqueness theorem, this formula requires no nondegeneracy assumption; it also requires no positivity or separate global regularity of g. It is a conditional identity for supplied connection data at x, not construction or global uniqueness of a connection.
